data.raw_text:
my response to Dr. Nagl's' piece. 

before I go on, let me state from the jump that Nagl puts "Dr" in his handle, always a douche move. 
also, for this to make one lick of sense you need to read his piece, and Mike's. 

okay. Hold my beer.

first, Nagl, excuse me Dr Nagl has a limited view of what constitutes "victory". By his logic we did not "win" the cold war, since we did not march on Moscow, and institute conditions similar to post-war Germany and Japan. You know, the little things. The GWOT victories are in the mosaic form. the failures stark. 

let me back up--stream of consciousness, motherfucker.

I've read every book Nagl has written when I was writing my Master's thesis on the Rhodesian Bush War. And damn, does he just keep on missing that mark. it was obvious that he was a former Armor Branch officer. Bold font, all caps Armor. Branch. Officer. TL;dr: one must win, and win a certain fashion, the right way. Think of some has-been on ESPN claiming that a team won, but they won is despite of establishing the ground game. Got me? Yeah? Moving on. 

How did you know that, Byrd? Because those guys are so welded to BIG ARMY doctrine one can see the routing seams in their writing. they are inflexible in thought and action(more on action later), the antithesis of airborne troops( to the uninitiated their thinking follows the logic of "well, we landed 40 kilometers from the DZ, we are armed with just purple dildos while the enemy is carrying  lethal pulse energy weapons. Cool. Rally on me, we will figure this shit out on the march." Why are they armed with purple dildos? Don't worry about it. 

okay. back to the response. 

Nagl knocks Mike on Mike's claim that the general public is ignorant about war. Y'all are. "But we aren't", y'all might say. alright. give me three sentences on each of the following topics
1. Infantry Battle in Classical Greece
2. the scope and mission of MACV-SOG

don't hang your heads, I'm ignorant of a heaping mess of things. Shit, my command of the English language is middling, at best, as I will prove going forward

Nagl writes that y'all have a "visceral sense about what constitutes a war". visceral, relating to deep inward feelings rather than to the intellect. I thought we live in a "fuck your feelings" world? No? did I miss a memo? 

Moving on. 

Nagl limits his scope to the "five biggest wars of the past eighty years". Narrows his scope, alright, and hides from you the "small wars". But I'm sure you can list the small wars of the last eighty years off-hand because you are not ignorant. Oh. 

let's break down the outcome of those wars(according to Nagl, sorry Dr Nagl), shall we? Not we, me, you guys have no idea what you are talking about. I say that with love. no I don't. 

Korea: he marks that one a tie. Look up Battle of the Pusan Perimeter, and then look at the end state of the war. Let me concede that the war was a "tie", it was not, it would have been a win if Douglas MacArthur did not step on his dick at near every turn. MacArthur is the sort of "winning" general that dudes like Nagl jerk off to with a belt around their necks. 
Vietnam: marks that one a loss. prima facie(LATIN!) it was a loss. UNTIL one views the war as a campaign of the Cold War. Again, mosaic. Vietnam was proof to CHINA we would take casualties in the defense of allies, and it informed would be allies that they would face a better outcome if they partnered with us. an aside: Ford should have bombed the hell out the NVA as they drove south like John Paul Vann(you know of him, because you are not ignorant--I promise I will stop with this trope) would have wanted. Vietnam, coupled with Nixon's brilliant handling of CHINA helped thaw(some say wrecked) the relationship between the USSR and the PRC. To this day Russia and CHINA are wary of one another. "But, Putin/Xi love feast Byrd?" Yeah, take a look at the strategic bombing stances of those two nations, then, you know, get back to me. 

Desert Storm: tallies that one a win. guess that is one in a row for Nagl. Did we throw the Kurds under the bus in that win, you bet, that did not come back to bite us in the ass, no sir, not at all. 

AFG, which he lists out of order, since we lost that one AFTER we "lost" Iraq: yeah that one...was not great. If I had if I had my druthers, we would have kicked Al-Qaeda in the sack, nullified the Taliban, and helped install a Peshmerga, then gotten out toot sweet, circa 2005~. Alas we did not go that route. I lost friends, Mike lost friends. Buuuuuuttttt, we did take a lot of bad dudes off the board. Don't worry, they had it coming. Also, Also, AFG is not really a country, it is a collection of counties. All praise to Gust Avrakotos for minting that line. Don't know of Gust, I betcha. 

 I must add this: Biden lost AFG. His first mistake in foreign policy in the last 40 years, so give him some slack. Google Biden+Bob Gates.

Iraq: counts that one as a loss. question, is the Ba'ath Party still a running things in Iraq? Saddam Hussein galavanting about? Nope. Nope. did we fuck up the prize to come of insurgency. Oh hell yeah, until about 2008/9.

Long time, for by God sure. Take a look at the US "occupation"of the Philippines. Look at the timeline. Look at the cost in lives. Not whataboutism, y'all need to be supplied a point of reference. 

I've visited Baghdad in the last year, pretty sure we won. Hey, if Nagl can interject appeals to emotion, he left the door open, and I will Ricky Recon my was through.

Then he slaps on how OIF and the challenges to follow, emboldened Iran, and made mess of Syria. Iran has been exposed as a paper tiger in a conventional sense, and Syria was having a couple of three troubles before Mike and I cross the LOD in March of '03--little bit of correlation-causation failures in Nagl's thinking

Okay. Let is come to a close and talk about Nagl's writing, and application of his thinking.

Most of his core cannon dates back over 20 years ago, his work that follows uses those first texts as a bedrock. Even the U.S. Army/Marine Corps Counterinsurgency Field Manual was written in late 2005. How do I know that, because I am a sneaky fuck, and a dude who knows people who know people.  Need I say more? 

Actions, I told you we would return to action, he has limited experience in the application of COIN. Mike on the other hand. Those that can't, teach, am I right? 

Oh, and the couple of lines that got my goat. Nagl notes that Mike sacrificed, and so did his brothers-in-arms. 

sacrificed. I cannot give a figure to the number of friends Mike lost. and Nagl drops this truth in, in the most blasé
 fashion, as if he is not other people to Mike. If I were on a panel with Nagl, sorry, DR Nagl, and he said such a thing, in the manner in which he wrote, we'd have more than words. 

anywho, I'm sure you are tried of reading this pissing-out-of-my-ass scattershot diatribe. 

In summation. Mike's piece good. Nagl's bad, and argued in bad faith. 

PS: you wanna read someone, read Bing West. And Mike, and Mike. to be sure. 

PSS: thoughts my own, I did not run a single word past Mike. if I had the syntax would be better, and the jokes MUCH funnier. 

All the Way! De Oppresso Liber! Spiritus Invictus!

The OASIS Schoolyards Project, by Resilient Cities Network (R-Cities) and the Temasek Foundation in partnership with the Quezon City government, aims to transform public school grounds into cooler, greener, and more climate-resilient spaces to protect students from extreme heat, flooding, and other climate risks.

Members of the Manila Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office conducted a flushing operation after a tanker truck carrying candy syrup spilled along Magsaysay Boulevard on Tuesday, Jan. 13. 

The cleanup was carried out to remove the sticky residue from the roadway, ensuring the safety of motorists and preventing further traffic disruption on the busy thoroughfare. 

📸: Mark Balmores/MB
